title: Learning millisecond protein dynamics from what is missing in NMR spectra.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded mBMRB/mBMRB.csv (2.5 MB), relaxdb/relaxdb_data.csv (1.0 MB) and relaxdb-cpmg_data.csv (5 KB) from the Hugging Face dataset (MIT licence, not gated); whole repo is 68 MB. mBMRB.csv has 9,786 rows: 231 malformed rows (empty id and label), and after removing those plus RelaxDB-style rows exactly 9,381 BMRB (Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank) entries remain, matching the paper. Per-residue label string has length equal to the sequence in every clean row; 1,072,373 residues, 12.2% marked missing. 1,011 sequences appear more than once; across 3,980 pairs of repeat depositions of the identical sequence, per-residue agreement is 0.923 and mean Cohen's kappa (chance-corrected agreement) 0.645. RelaxDB: 133 proteins, 126 UniProt IDs, 16,255 residues (646 Rex '^', 749 missing, 140 mixed). CPMG set: 10 proteins, 1,916 residues. GitHub split files: train_30pc 6,572 ids, val 500, test 100, all present in the CSV; 80/50/30% sequence-identity cluster files exist. BMRB entry IDs in the data go up to 51871.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (paywalled, no PMCID in Europe PMC; PMC and bioRxiv full text blocked by captcha/HTTP 429). Dyna-1's AUROC/AUPRC numbers, the BMRB curation freeze date and the filter rules were not retrieved. That Dyna-1 is the best of several models, and that it predicts relaxation-measured exchange, comes from the abstract and README.

a1_downloadable.note: Public Hugging Face dataset, MIT licence, no login; CSVs downloaded directly (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Per-residue label string ('.' missing, 'A' assigned) is a column aligned to the sequence column (checked). RelaxDB exchange labels are also a column with a documented vocabulary.

a3_inputs_present.note: Amino-acid sequences are in the CSV, plus 811+ AlphaFold2 PDB files in mBMRB/pdbs (file listing seen, not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: Labels are categorical per residue with a documented vocabulary; RelaxDB has field_strength (MHz) and temp_K columns (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: 9,381 proteins / about 1.07 million labelled residues in mBMRB (counted). True dynamics labels (RelaxDB) are only 133 proteins, used for evaluation.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~4 MB of CSV; ESM-2 embeddings for ~1.07M residues at 1,280 dims would be ~5 GB float32, fine if stored per protein or with the 640-dim model
a6_fits_laptop.note: Frozen ESM-2 (a protein language model) embedding of 9,381 proteins of median 105 residues is CPU-feasible.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: After dropping 231 malformed rows and RelaxDB-vocabulary rows, exactly 9,381 entries, matching the paper's 9,381 (checked). RelaxDB 133 and CPMG 10 also match the README.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is whether the depositors assigned each backbone amide signal in BMRB: an experimental record, not a model output or computed from sequence. It is a noisy proxy for exchange (missing peaks also come from overlap, low signal-to-noise or incomplete work); the authors state this assumption.

B1.why: mBMRB is one 4-column CSV holding id, sequence, per-residue label and structure path (checked).

B2.why: Parses with pandas, but 231 rows have empty id/label and RelaxDB rows are mixed into mBMRB.csv (checked).

B3.why: One observable (assigned or not), but from thousands of labs, magnetic fields and conditions; RelaxDB mixes BMRB, digitised plots, tables.

B4.why: No censoring in mBMRB; RelaxDB has 'no data' classes (t, x) that must be masked, documented as -1 (checked).

B5.why: 1,011 sequences deposited more than once, 762 with differing labels (checked); cluster files make grouping easy.

B6.why: Hugging Face README documents every column and each label character's meaning (read).

C1.why: Testing Dyna-1 on later BMRB depositions, and the label noise ceiling, are informative whichever way they come out.

C2.why: One model for this task, Dyna-1 (open weights, cluster split); DynaProt-style models cover fast motions, not millisecond exchange.

C3.why: Re-evaluation angle: noise ceiling from repeat depositions plus temporal test; a modest 'Better' case, not novel data.

C4.why: Measuring exchange needs NMR relaxation dispersion experiments: isotope-labelled protein and days of spectrometer time.

C5.why: Amino-acid and secondary-structure frequency dummy baselines shipped (data/probs); Dyna-1 runnable via eval.py.

D1.why: ESM-2 open weights; Dyna-1 itself ships an ESM-2 variant (README).

D2.why: Per-residue embeddings cached once on CPU, then a small classifier head.

D3.why: ESM-2 MIT, data and code MIT; ESM-3 (Dyna-1's best backbone) is non-commercial but optional.

E1.why: 30%-identity cluster train/val/test split files provided on GitHub (checked); held-out RelaxDB proteins too.

E2.why: Thousands of sequence clusters; test 100 proteins, val 500 (counted).

E3.why: Per-amino-acid and per-secondary-structure missing rates computable; authors ship these as probs_aa/probs_dssp.

E4.why: 3,980 repeat-deposition pairs of identical sequences: kappa 0.645, agreement 0.923 (computed).

E5.why: N-terminal residue nearly always missing (seen in rows); authors report enzyme active sites well predicted.

E6.why: Label shuffling within protein and amino-acid-only ablation are straightforward on per-residue labels.

E7.why: RelaxDB (133) and CPMG (10) relaxation-measured labels; BMRB IDs allow a deposition-order split.

E8.why: Weights and eval.py public, so their RelaxDB numbers are reproducible; I did not retrieve the numbers.

G1.why: mBMRB has BMRB entry IDs and sequences, no UniProt; RelaxDB has UniProt (checked).

G2.why: BMRB itself: entries deposited after the freeze (IDs above 51871), joinable on BMRB ID.

G3.why: One row per BMRB entity ('_0', '_1' suffix), one label per residue.

G4.why: New depositions test generalisation forward in time; marginally bigger question than the original data.

H1.why: Both assigned and missing residues recorded for every protein (12.2% missing, counted).

H2.why: Thousands of labs, but BMRB favours small soluble proteins: median 105 residues, max 695 (counted).

H3.why: Claim stated below, limited to backbone-amide assignment gaps in small proteins someone chose to assign.

H4.why: Authors explicitly call missing-equals-exchange an assumption (abstract).

I1.why: Kern and Wayment-Steele labs; NMR groups choosing which residues to probe with relaxation dispersion.

I2.why: Calibrated per-residue confidence could change which proteins get costly dispersion experiments; marginal otherwise.

I3.why: PR-AUC (precision-recall area) roughly matches 'which residues to inspect'; true decision is top-k residues.

I4.why: Amino-acid/terminus rules capture part of the signal; how much remains is unverified.

J1.why: Real per-residue modelling, grouped splits, calibration, transfer to relaxation labels.

J2.why: NMR intuition needed to judge exchange plausibility; some checks (termini, prolines, loops) are intuitive.

J3.why: Noise-ceiling analysis alone is shareable before any model is trained.

J5.why: Kill condition below; date not yet written in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: Dyna-1 (this paper; ESM-3 intermediate layer plus head, also ESM-2 and AF2 variants)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on mBMRB with 30%-identity cluster splits (train 6,572 / val 500 / test 100, files checked), evaluated on held-out RelaxDB and CPMG proteins; AUROC/AUPRC values not retrieved (paper paywalled, preprint blocked).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Assumes missing assignments mean exchange; extending to side chains, larger proteins and raw spectra was named as future work (secondary newsletter summary, not the paper).

existing_models.name: DynaProt (Bafna, Jing, Berger, ICLR 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicts fast-timescale flexibility (RMSF, covariances) from molecular dynamics; not the millisecond exchange task.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (650M or 150M checkpoint), frozen per-residue embeddings
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU, ~1 h embedding for 9,381 proteins with 650M (estimate)

integration.partner_dataset: BMRB entries deposited after the mBMRB curation freeze (entry IDs above 51871 and later 30000-series), labelled with the same missing-assignment rule
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a model trained on past NMR depositions predict which residues will go missing in proteins deposited later, beyond what repeat-deposition noise allows?

controls.positive_control: N-terminal residue almost always missing (seen in rows); per-amino-acid baseline must be recovered; Dyna-1's own RelaxDB number reproduced with eval.py.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels within each protein and confirm PR-AUC collapses to the per-protein missing fraction; amino-acid-identity-only model.
controls.external_validation: RelaxDB (133 proteins, relaxation-measured exchange) and RelaxDB-CPMG (10); post-freeze BMRB depositions as a temporal set.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts which backbone amide signals depositors failed to assign in small soluble proteins in BMRB, a noisy proxy for millisecond exchange whose repeat-deposition agreement (kappa 0.645) caps achievable accuracy.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's amino-acid sequence to predict which residues will be invisible in NMR spectra, a sign of slow motion.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-residue embeddings of 9,381 NMR-studied proteins (about 1.07 million residues), each residue tagged assigned or missing.
plain_idea.predict: The probability that each residue's backbone signal is missing from the deposited NMR assignment, checked against relaxation experiments that directly measure slow exchange in 133 proteins.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: NMR labs could pick which proteins and residues deserve week-long relaxation experiments; and the repeat-deposition analysis tells everyone how good any such model can possibly be.

more_or_better_data.why: Dyna-1 used all 9,381 curated entries up to its freeze (max BMRB ID 51871); only post-freeze BMRB depositions, number unverified, would add data.

confidence_score.why: 3,980 repeat-deposition pairs give a measured label-noise level (kappa 0.645); Dyna-1 outputs probabilities but, as far as I saw, no calibration against this noise.

models_beatable.why: Dyna-1 is 2026, pretrained ESM-3 backbone, cluster-split evaluation: hard to beat on its own test; its test set is only 100 proteins, so re-evaluation is feasible.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Post-freeze BMRB entries measure the same quantity but must be labelled with the authors' curation filters, which I didn't verify reproduce, so 'same measurement, same way' is not guaranteed.

label_elsewhere.sources: BMRB (known resource) holds assignment completeness for further entries beyond the 9,381; RelaxDB's relaxation Rex labels exist only for 133 proteins (counted).
label_elsewhere.join_key: BMRB entry ID; UniProt for RelaxDB
label_elsewhere.why: New BMRB depositions give a forward-in-time test set, but each needs re-deriving the missing-assignment label.

risks: The same protein deposited several times (1,011 repeated sequences) could land in train and test, letting the model memorise its missing residues.
Homologous proteins and mutant series share missing patterns; a random split would leak through sequence similarity.
RelaxDB proteins are also in mBMRB (all 133 sequences found), so training on their mBMRB labels then testing on RelaxDB leaks.
Lab-specific habits (e.g. not assigning termini or tags) correlate with label and could be learned as shortcuts.
leakage_plan.split: Use the authors' 30%-identity cluster split (train_30pc/val/test files, checked) and drop all RelaxDB sequences from training; add a temporal split by BMRB entry ID (id column, checked).
checks: Shuffle labels within each protein; PR-AUC must fall to the per-protein missing fraction.
Nearest-neighbour sequence identity of each test protein to training; report performance by identity bin.
Model using only amino-acid identity and position-from-terminus; the learned model must clearly beat it.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: cluster files and the RelaxDB overlap are known and easy to exclude.

success_criteria.metric: Per-residue PR-AUC (precision-recall area under the curve) on RelaxDB exchange labels, because the user wants the residues most likely to show exchange.
success_criteria.baselines: Per-amino-acid missing frequency from mBMRB train (authors' probs_aa); Dyna-1 ESM-2 and ESM-3 versions run via eval.py. Their published numbers were not retrieved.
success_criteria.success: Frozen ESM-2 head within 0.02 PR-AUC of Dyna-1 on RelaxDB and on post-freeze BMRB entries, with calibrated probabilities (expected calibration error below the amino-acid baseline's). Exact thresholds await reproducing Dyna-1's numbers.
success_criteria.noise_ceiling: Repeat depositions of identical sequences agree with Cohen's kappa 0.645 (mean, 3,980 pairs) and 92.3% per-residue agreement (computed).
success_criteria.kill: If fewer than 300 post-freeze BMRB proteins pass the filters, or the ESM-2 head is no better than the amino-acid baseline by 0.05 PR-AUC after one week, stop.

ambitious.why: Would need a clear temporal-generalisation result plus a noise ceiling showing Dyna-1 sits near or far from it.

realistic.why: Publishes re-evaluations and benchmarks; a noise ceiling plus temporal test of Dyna-1 fits.

fallback.journal: bioRxiv preprint plus MLSB (Machine Learning in Structural Biology) workshop
fallback.why: Even a 'labels are too noisy' result is a useful short note.

pitch.headline: 9,381 NMR-studied proteins with per-residue labels, MIT-licensed, plus 3,980 repeat depositions that measure label noise directly.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Repeat depositions of identical sequences give a measured ceiling (kappa 0.645) that few per-residue biology labels have; 1.07 million labelled residues; relaxation-measured test set of 133 proteins.
pitch.the_win: Show Dyna-1's accuracy on post-freeze BMRB depositions relative to the 0.645-kappa noise ceiling, with calibrated per-residue confidence from a CPU-only ESM-2 head.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: The noise ceiling alone tells the field how much better any missing-assignment model can get.
pitch.who_wants_it: Kern and Wayment-Steele labs and NMR groups choosing which proteins get relaxation dispersion experiments.

ml_idea: Freeze ESM-2, train a per-residue head on mBMRB with the authors' 30% cluster split, calibrate it, and compare against Dyna-1 and amino-acid baselines on RelaxDB and on newer BMRB depositions, framed against the noise ceiling from repeat depositions.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: 9,381 proteins of median 105 residues with ESM-2 650M at ~0.5 s each on CPU; head is a small classifier on cached embeddings. Building the post-freeze BMRB set adds an estimated 1-2 days.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count BMRB protein entries deposited after the freeze (IDs above 51871 plus later 30000-series) that have 15N backbone assignments and under 30% identity to mBMRB train; need at least 300.

verdict_reason: Clean, MIT-licensed, counts match exactly (9,381), and repeat depositions give a measured noise ceiling; but the only model, Dyna-1, is open and recent, so the project rests on a temporal test whose size (post-freeze BMRB entries) is unverified.
